explanations.3: This tells Ubuntu's package installer to run without asking for user input (noninteractive mode), which is necessary in Docker since there's no terminal to respond to prompts.
explanations.7: The sed command is modifying Ubuntu's package source list to unlock additional software repositories (universe and multiverse contain community-maintained packages that aren't enabled by default).
explanations.13: Deleting the cached package lists saves space in the Docker image since we won't need them again after installation.
explanations.31: The printf command is writing a multi-line JavaScript function into a file; the backslash-n creates actual line breaks in the file.
explanations.34: This sed command modifies the file to create a difference that git will track, so when you run git diff later, there's an actual change to display.
explanations.39: This adds a custom shell prompt (PS1) that will show a whale emoji and color codes when you open a bash shell, making it visually clear you're inside a container.
